title: Fixture: third, listed first in ORDER
role: You are on call for a small web team (test fixture, not a real incident).
brief: The disk alert for `web1.example.com` fires at 97% on `/var`. Priya asks in the team channel whether anyone changed logging. Text with a tag that must stay text: not bold & more.

steps.situation: The site still answers, slowly. Where is the space going?
steps.evidence:
$ df -h /var
Filesystem  Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sdb1    20G   19G  640M  97% /var

choices.why: You find one 14 GB log file in a minute and know what to fix.

choices.text: Tell the channel it is probably the new hire's change
choices.why: Guessing out loud about a person costs trust and finds nothing.

choices.text: Reboot the server to clear temporary files
choices.why: An outage for nothing: the log is still there after the reboot.

choices.text: Ask Sam, who set up logging, what changed
choices.why: A fair question that keeps the team in the loop, but you still need to measure.

steps.situation: The 14 GB file is the application log, still open by the service.

choices.text: Truncate it in place and keep the last lines
choices.why: Space comes back at once and the service keeps writing.
The space stays used while the service holds the file open, and the evidence is gone.
You turned a disk warning into a weekend outage.

steps.situation: Space is back. How do you stop this happening again?

choices.text: Add a logrotate rule, test it with `logrotate -d`, and write a short incident note
choices.why: The fix is tested and the team knows what happened.

choices.text: Add a nightly cron job that empties the log
choices.why: It keeps the disk free but throws away every day's evidence.

choices.text: Do nothing: it took a year to fill
choices.why: It will fill again, at a worse moment.

debrief.what_happened: In this fixture the application log had no rotation rule, so it grew for a year until `/var` filled. The team truncated it in place, added a logrotate rule and checked it with a dry run. See [the module](01-storage-disk.md) too.
lessons: Measure with df and du before deleting anything.
Truncate an open log; rm does not free the space while it is open.
Test a logrotate rule with a dry run.
